newsitem.title: USA: Hunt to get M.L. Cass stake for acreage.
newsitem.headline: Hunt to get M.L. Cass stake for acreage.

text.p: M. L. Cass Petroleum Corp said Wednesday it signed a letter of intent with Nelson Bunker Hunt and affiliated companies to explore for oil and gas in Australia, Pakistan and Turkey.

The company said it will acquire interests in nine concessions covering over 11.6 million acres and will be offered the rights during the next six months to participate in future concessions obtained by Hunt.
In return, Hunt and Hemco C.V. will acquire 46 percent of Cass' common and 40 percent of the company's interest in any finds after recovery of exploration costs, it said.
Hunt's fortune traces back to the 1930 "Black Giant" oil field discovery in East Texas, purchased by Nelson Bunker's father -- H.L. Hunt -- for $1.3 million.

By 1980, the family fortune was estimated at $5.1 billion. But a $134.6 million judgement resulting from attempts to corner the silver market in 1980 forced Nelson Bunker and his brother, William Herbert, to file for bankruptcy in September 1990.
Hunt's bankruptcy case, with debts of about $500 million and assets of about $100 million, was the largest personal bankruptcy case in U.S. history.
Settlements left him with few assets except his house, furnishings and two aging cars, though other family members, many of them millionaires, provided him with a comfortable lifestyle.
Cass Petroleum said it will issue 14 million common shares to Hunt, the corporations in which he owns an interest and Hemco.
Hemco owns the Pakastani concessions being acquired and is controlled by Hunt, M. L. Cass President Michael Cass said.
Cass Petroleum said it now has 13,858,165 fully diluted shares outstanding.
After the issuance and exercise of the shares and share warrants granted for this transaction, it will have 30,270,165 fully diluted shares outstanding.

The company said the transaction is subject to satisfactory due diligence reviews by each of the parties, reaching definitive agreements and the receipt of all necessary regulatory and third party approvals.

As a condition of the letter of intent, Michael Cass will remain president, chief executive officer and a director of the company and Hunt will be elected to the board as chairman. The other three existing directors have agreed to step down.
Michael Cass said he and Hunt will each name three directors and, in event of a tie vote, Hunt will have the deciding vote.
A special shareholders meeting of will be held to vote on the transaction and elect the new six member board.

The company said Temple Securities (Canada) Ltd will assist in raising the capital to fund the first phase of seismic and exploratory drilling on the nine blocks and to fund the company's efforts to secure several other large concessions currently being negotiated in other countries.
Michael Cass said he expects the company will have to raise between $30 and $100 million with equity sales to fund these activities, adding much of it is expected to be raised in Europe.

The company said the first exploratory well will be drilled in Australia during November of this year utilizing a rig being shipped from Houston and a second exploratory well is scheduled to be drilled in Pakistan during February 1997.
